clue.text: Mark has a fresh hope — to restrict bad temper

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so the shuffled letters close around the bad temper
fresh means new, so the word hope is made anew in a different order

parts.note: a strop is a fit of bad temper

explanation.surface: Someone hopeful is trying to keep their temper in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' rearranges the four letters into POHE; a strop is British slang for a sulk or tantrum.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostrophe is a punctuation mark, the raised comma used in contractions and possessives.

clue.text: Plant deal splashed outside new shop

indicators.note: outside means the first group of letters goes around the second
splashed suggests something thrown about, so the letters of deal are scattered
new signals the letters of shop are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A retailer has announced a big deal at a newly opened shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Two anagrams, each with its own indicator: 'splashed' gives ADEL and 'new' gives SPHO, which ADEL wraps after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The asphodel is a lily-family flower, famed in Greek myth as the bloom of the underworld meadows.

clue.text: Car lacks energy? It may give one a bitter experience

definitions.text: It may give one a bitter experience

indicators.note: lacks says the car's name is missing a letter

parts.note: a Citroen is a French make of car
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A car that has run out of power gives its owner a sour experience.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a whimsical description: the fruit is sour to taste.
explanation.definitionFit: The citron is a large, thick-skinned citrus fruit whose sour, bitter flesh is mainly candied for peel.

clue.text: Queen cheated, ending with nothing

indicators.note: ending with places the second piece at the end of the first

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat them, so did means cheated
O is the round figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A monarch was a fraud and finished with nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Dido was the legendary founding queen of Carthage, abandoned by Aeneas in Virgil's epic.

clue.text: Like virgin territory with mud planter managed

indicators.note: managed means handled or arranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Untouched land is being looked after by a gardener who works the mud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'managed' rearranges MUD PLANTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground nobody has walked over is untrodden, just as virgin territory is unexplored.

clue.text: A superior blast associated with a name such as Pope or Swift

parts.note: U stands for upper-class, i.e. superior
a gust is a blast of wind

explanation.surface: A grand gust of wind is linked to a famous name.
explanation.walkthrough: Pope and Swift are not a pontiff and a bird but the writers Alexander Pope and Jonathan Swift.
explanation.definitionFit: Augustan describes the early-18th-century English literary age of Pope, Swift and Addison.

clue.text: Fine list of items missing the last bit — the bit that doesn't matter

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: missing the last bit tells us to drop the final letter of the word for a list

parts.note: an agenda is a list of items for a meeting

explanation.surface: A meeting's agenda trails off, and the last item is the one that never matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing the last bit' trims AGENDA to AGEND.
explanation.definitionFit: A fag end, British slang for a cigarette stub, is a useless leftover remnant.

clue.text: Trees beginning to be cut

indicators.note: to be cut means the word is shortened, losing its tail

parts.note: first means beginning, as in the first steps

explanation.surface: Woodcutters are about to start felling trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be cut' docks the final T from FIRST.
explanation.definitionFit: Firs are evergreen conifers, a common kind of tree.

clue.text: Place one surrendered to accommodate one novice driver as carriage guide

indicators.note: to accommodate means to take in, so the remaining letters house the next ones
surrendered means given up, so the word for place gives up a letter

parts.note: a position is a place
I is the Roman numeral for one
I is the Roman numeral for one
L is the learner-driver plate

explanation.surface: A post handed over to a learner driver who is to steer a carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrendered' drops an I from POSITION to leave POSTION, then 'to accommodate' takes in IL.
explanation.definitionFit: A postilion rides the leading horse of a team to steer a horse-drawn coach.

clue.text: This writer's a Greek character, seen in retrospect as having some taste

indicators.note: in retrospect means looking back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: the setter refers to themself; this writer is I'm, I am
mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: The setter claims to be a Greek figure who, on reflection, has good taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in retrospect' reads the pieces backwards, so the setter's I'M ends the answer rather than starting it.
explanation.definitionFit: Umami is the savoury fifth basic taste, alongside sweet, sour, salt and bitter.

clue.text: Namely, that female's getting cross in one fast movement

parts.note: sc. (scilicet) is the Latin abbreviation for namely
her is that female, the 's being a link
a zo (or dzo) is a cross between a yak and a cow

explanation.surface: A woman is getting angry in one quick motion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like 'angry' but means a hybrid animal: the zo, a yak-cow cross bred in the Himalayas.
explanation.definitionFit: A scherzo is a lively, quick movement in a symphony or sonata.

clue.text: Bringer of news speaks again, wasting little time

indicators.note: wasting means using up and losing, so one letter disappears

parts.note: to reutter is to speak again
T is a short abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A newsreader repeats themselves and squanders the brief time available.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasting' takes one T out of REUTTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Reuters is an international news agency supplying stories to the media.

clue.text: Person of recognised art, like Pasquale? I'm hot!

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist of recognised standing
Pasquale is the setter Don Manley, and Don Pasquale an opera, so he is a don

explanation.surface: An acclaimed artist, like the setter, boasts of being attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot' is slang for radioactive; the gas boasts it is hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Radon is a radioactive gas, and hot is slang for dangerously radioactive.

clue.text: Cooked meat's done for worms

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are worked over into a new form

explanation.surface: Meat that is properly cooked is safe from worms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked' rearranges MEATS DONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nematodes are roundworms, many of them parasites in undercooked meat.

clue.text: One from Central America rushin' up, pursued by an exotic bird

indicators.note: pursued by means followed by, so the next pieces come after
in a down clue up means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: rushing is racing; with its g dropped, racin'
the guan is a tropical American game bird

explanation.surface: A Central American man hurries off, chased by an unusual bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses RACIN to NICAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nicaraguan is a native of Nicaragua, a country in Central America.

clue.text: Devilish type established in bishop's place, male showing feeling of confidence

indicators.note: in places the devilish one and the established one inside the bishop's seat

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese
an elf is a mischievous sprite

explanation.surface: An impish figure installed in a cathedral post shows a man's self-assurance.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-esteem is confidence in one's own worth.

clue.text: As an activist, could I be inimical at a poll that goes the wrong way?

indicators.note: going the wrong way means going awry, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A campaigner wonders whether a disastrous election result could turn them hostile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that goes the wrong way' rearranges INIMICAL AT A POLL; 'could I be' just links the definition to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A political animal is someone who relishes politics and campaigning, as an activist does.

clue.text: Like a piece of paper that could express a finely balanced argument?

definitions.text: Like a piece of paper that could express a finely balanced argument?

parts.words: Like a piece of paper that could express a finely balanced argument
parts.note: paper has a front and back, and an argument with merit on each side has the same property

explanation.walkthrough: A sheet has two faces, and a balanced argument presents both cases.
explanation.definitionFit: Two-sided means having two faces, or treating both points of view in a debate.

clue.text: Maiden having opportunity to discard old slipper

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

indicators.note: to discard means to throw away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: an occasion is an opportunity

explanation.surface: A young woman gets a chance to throw away her old slipper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to discard' drops O from OCCASION.
explanation.definitionFit: A moccasin is a soft leather shoe, often worn as a slipper.

clue.text: Besotted girl bewailed losing knight

parts.note: Ena is a girl's name

indicators.note: losing means going without, so one letter is taken away

parts.note: to bewail is to mourn
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A lovestruck girl lamented the loss of her knight in shining armour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes N from MOURNED.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamoured means filled with love; besotted means infatuated.

clue.text: Number in a location for biblical sermon

parts.note: Jesus preached the Sermon on the Mount

explanation.surface: A tally of people attending a famous scriptural sermon.
explanation.definitionFit: An amount is a quantity or total, a number.

clue.text: 'Shut up!', said the philosopher

indicators.note: said signals that the word is pronounced, giving one of the same sound

parts.note: to lock is to shut up securely

explanation.surface: A philosopher is ordered to keep quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shut up!' looks like a demand for silence but means to secure.
explanation.definitionFit: John Locke was a 17th-century English empiricist philosopher.

clue.text: Gift on bill — pay finally

parts.note: in cricket the on side is the leg side
AC is short for account, a bill

indicators.note: finally means take the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A present arrives with an invoice: pay at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A legacy is money or property left as a gift in a will.

clue.text: What rowdy republican might do with reservation

definitions.meaning: a noisy anti-monarchist might jeer the monarch

explanation.surface: A rowdy anti-monarchist voices their doubts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reservation' looks like 'misgiving' but is a reserved seat or table.
explanation.definitionFit: A booking is an advance arrangement for a seat, room or table.

clue.text: Biscuit expert?

definitions.meaning: ... and biscuit are both pale yellowish-brown colours

explanation.walkthrough: 'Biscuit' is the colour, not the snack.
explanation.definitionFit: Buff is a light brownish-yellow shade, and also a knowledgeable fan.

clue.text: Traveller in Russian plane to hold forth

parts.note: the MiG is a Russian military jet
to rant is to hold forth at length

explanation.surface: A passenger on a Russian jet is about to start lecturing.
explanation.definitionFit: A migrant is a person or creature that travels to settle or live elsewhere.

clue.text: Wizardry of a long-distance runner on run not last!

parts.note: Mo Farah is a British Olympic long-distance champion

indicators.note: not last means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to jog is to run gently

explanation.surface: An endurance runner's magic lies in not finishing last.
explanation.walkthrough: Mo Farah won Olympic gold at 5,000m and 10,000m for Britain. 'not last' trims JOG to JO.
explanation.definitionFit: Mojo means magic charm or power, a kind of wizardry.

clue.text: Crime of escaping criminal

indicators.note: escaping means getting out, so those letters leave

parts.note: an offence is a crime

explanation.surface: Breaking out is a crime for any lawbreaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crime of escaping' reads as a charge, but 'of' is the piece that escapes from OFFENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A fence is a criminal who handles and sells on stolen goods.

clue.text: Word that describes a den that's black inside, cold inside

indicators.note: inside puts the black piece within the den

parts.note: a dive is a seedy den or bar

indicators.note: inside here puts cold within the black piece

parts.note: jet is a deep black

explanation.surface: Someone describes a dark, chilly den.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective is a part of speech that qualifies or modifies a noun.
